plan: [With value $48 and three-bidder rule where the winner pays the lowest (third-highest) bid, bidding my true value maximizes win probability while guaranteeing I never pay more than my value. Bidding above $48 risks the rare event both opponents bid >$48, producing a negative payoff. Since values are uniform and >$48 is extremely unlikely, submit bid = $48 to maximize long-run expected profit while avoiding downside risk.]

[In a 3-bidder third-price auction the winner pays the lowest opponent bid. Assuming opponents bid their values (uniform 0–49), expected utility for a bid b is (b/49)^2*(v - b/3), maximized at b* = min(2v,49). With my value v=38, 2v=76>49 so the constrained optimum is b=49. Bidding the maximum wins with high probability while the expected minimum opponent bid stays below my value, maximizing expected profit under these assumptions.]

[With value $12 and no history, assume opponents bid their values (iid Uniform[0,49]). In this third-price auction, if I bid B, win prob ≈ (B/49)^2 and expected payment conditional on winning ≈ B/3, so expected profit ∝ B^2(12 − B/3). Maximizing that gives B=24. Bid $24 to balance win probability and the expected third-price payment, maximizing expected profit under this symmetric assumption.]
